why:
phase-427 W10 (2026-09-08) — LANDED. `Context::create_executor_in<'b>(&self, backing: &'b mut [MaybeUninit<u64>]) -> Result<Executor<'b>, InitError>` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs`, `rmw-cffi`): `create_executor` with the storage supplied by the caller instead of leaked. The returned executor BORROWS the backing for `'b` rather than living forever, so an RTOS or bare-metal entry that owns a `static mut [MaybeUninit<u64>; N]` — or the array `nros::main!` sizes for it — opens a session with no allocation at all.

NO DISPOSITION IS WRITTEN. The four dispositions are what clause 1 does to a CANDIDATE FROM CLAUSE 2 (RFC-0089); rclrs allocates its executor and has no counterpart for handing one storage, so there is nothing here for a constraint to permit, weaken or refuse. Same reasoning as `rust:init_with_launch`.

What it adds over the `unsafe Executor::open_in` it wraps is the LENGTH CHECK: `backing.len() < ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT.u64_len()` is `InitError::BackingTooSmall { needed, given }` naming both numbers, so the one precondition that makes `open_in` `unsafe` is enforced rather than documented. The refusal runs BEFORE the RMW is consulted, which is a property with a test (`packages/testing/nros-tests/tests/context_create_executor.rs`): with the order reversed, a caller whose `static` is short would be told the router is missing.

The `needed` figure moves with `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_CBS` / `_MAX_SC` / `_ARENA_SIZE` / `_MAX_NODES`, so the doc comment says to size the array from `ExecutorSizing::DEFAULT.u64_len()` and never from a literal.
